label: Information Theory
shortDescription: The mathematical study of the quantification, storage, and communication of information.
modulesDescription: Read the information-theory chapters in order, or jump directly to the topic you need.
ogTitle: Learn Information Theory for Free | CalcPath
ogDescription: Master entropy, mutual information, source and channel coding, rate-distortion theory, network information theory, and advanced topics like quantum information and Kolmogorov complexity — with detailed explanations, worked examples, and practice questions.
courseDescription: A complete information theory course covering foundations of entropy and information measures, source coding and data compression algorithms, channel coding and error correction, rate-distortion theory, network information theory, and advanced topics including quantum information theory, algorithmic information theory, secret sharing, and differential privacy. Features ELI5 intuition, step-by-step worked examples, common mistakes, and hundreds of practice problems.

topics.title: Entropy, Joint and Conditional Entropy
topics.description: What information means, how entropy measures it, and how entropy behaves when several random variables are considered together.

topics.title: Mutual Information and Relative Entropy
topics.description: How much one variable says about another, how far one distribution sits from another, and the inequalities that tie the two together.

topics.title: Entropy Rates and the AEP
topics.description: Information per symbol for a process with memory, and the asymptotic equipartition property that makes long sequences predictable in bulk.

topics.title: Source Coding and the Entropy Bound
topics.description: Shannon's source coding theorem in both directions, and Kraft's inequality — why entropy is the floor no lossless code can beat.

topics.title: Huffman and Shannon–Fano Codes
topics.description: Building an optimal prefix code symbol by symbol, proving it optimal, and seeing where the older Shannon–Fano construction falls short.

topics.title: Arithmetic, Lempel–Ziv and Universal Coding
topics.description: Coding a whole message as one interval, learning the dictionary as you go, and what it costs to compress a source you were not told about.

topics.title: Channel Capacity and the Coding Theorem
topics.description: How much a noisy channel can carry, the proof that the rate is achievable, and why feedback does not raise it.

topics.title: Linear and Hamming Codes
topics.description: Minimum distance, the bounds it must obey, and the classical linear constructions that correct errors by syndrome.

topics.title: Modern Codes: LDPC, Polar and Turbo
topics.description: The sparse-graph and polarization constructions that finally reach capacity in practice, and how they are decoded.

topics.title: Rate–Distortion Theory
topics.description: The best rate achievable at a given distortion, computed in closed form where it can be and numerically where it cannot.

topics.title: Quantization
topics.description: Turning the theory into a codebook: scalar quantizers, the Lloyd–Max conditions, and why quantizing vectors beats quantizing one sample at a time.

topics.title: Distributed Source Coding and Side Information
topics.description: Compressing correlated sources that cannot talk to each other — Slepian–Wolf, Wyner–Ziv, and the binning argument behind both.

topics.title: Multiple-Access and Broadcast Channels
topics.description: Many senders into one receiver, and one sender to many receivers: capacity regions rather than a single number.

topics.title: Network Coding and Common Randomness
topics.description: Mixing packets inside the network instead of forwarding them, and distilling shared secrecy from correlated observations.

topics.title: Algorithmic Information Theory
topics.description: Kolmogorov complexity: the information in a single object, its relationship to entropy, and the results its uncomputability forces.

topics.title: Quantum Information
topics.description: Qubits and density matrices, von Neumann entropy, the Holevo bound, and what entanglement adds that no classical resource can.

topics.title: Secret Sharing and Secure Computation
topics.description: Splitting a secret so that any t shares reveal it and any t−1 reveal nothing, and computing on data nobody is allowed to see.

topics.title: Differential Privacy
topics.description: A guarantee stated as a divergence bound, the mechanisms that meet it, and what composition costs across repeated queries.
